judgment: Both attempts make genuine links to topics and methods. The closest adds European legal institutions and public economics, which are stronger than general creative work for the target. European integration, German Expressionism, modern warfare and the Frankfurt School provide substantive partial coverage. Their combined contribution does not supply a continuing Germany-centred inquiry. The related arts route is coherent but does not supply a sustained German literary or cultural corpus. The language inquiry is independent of this primary judgment.

HCBCOGN312.contribution: Studies language processing and acquisition from cognitive and neurological perspectives. It provides neither German practice nor contrastive German grammar.
HCBCOGN312.topics: Psycholinguistics is the study of the neurobiological and psychological factors that enable us to acquire, use, and understand language. Modern research draws on cognitive psychology, neuroscience, and computer science to investigate how language is processed. The course focuses primarily, though not exclusively, on the neuroscience of language. Students examine theoretical and experimental issues in speech production and comprehension, language impairments, the relationship between thought and language, and the evolution and acquisition of language. They also gain hands-on experience with experimental approaches to the study of language and develop an understanding of human linguistic capacity as a subject of multidisciplinary research. Topics covered: What is language? Evolutionary aspects of language and animal communication; language and thought; aphasia; language acquisition; bilingualism; speech comprehension; semantics; reading and dyslexia; speech production.

adjudication: Archived canonical failed two current offering checks. Revised schedules mechanically close, including Psycholinguistics after its gateway in the first available spring. No-match follows content review of the repaired plans.

candidateAssessments.concept: Germany in European history, politics and society
candidateAssessments.assessment: The revised plan includes war and historical change, comparative institutions, EU politics and law, public economics, migration, propaganda and environmental justice. European integration and German historical episodes give real bridges. The taught curriculum lacks connected study of the German state, political economy, migration and public debates across periods. The law and economics courses offer comparative frameworks without a continuing German application.

candidateAssessments.concept: German literature, film and cultural identity
candidateAssessments.assessment: Film and Media includes German Expressionism, and Western Art History and documentary provide related European context. World literature, adaptation, stylistics, memoir and gender history support specific methods and themes. The portfolio does not sustain a sequence of German literature, film or cultural criticism and has no documented recurring German-language corpus.

candidateAssessments.concept: German language, linguistics and academic writing
candidateAssessments.assessment: Psycholinguistics examines processing and acquisition, Style & Meaning studies form and interpretation, and introductory Dutch offers a related West Germanic language. None teaches German reading, grammar, writing or speech, or analyses German and Dutch systematically in contrast. A German language-centred pathway cannot be assembled.

courseScreen: Reviewed active course titles, profiles, topics, methods and descriptions for German-speaking society, history, art, politics, language and plausible complementary work. Considered introductory Dutch as a contrastive lead and considered historical research and modern art as substitute leads. The research seminar is centred on the American century. Modern Art & Modern Museums surveys a wide range of movements and exhibition practices. Neither adds a dedicated Germany sequence. There is no course taught as German proficiency or contrastive German linguistics.
